parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a comparatively benign state with a hostile federal layer. State level: no facility or sex-definition law, vetoed care and sports bans, an inclusive 2019 executive order, tolerant polling, a July 2026 low-risk grouping — but no statewide gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage. Federal level drives exposure: visa refusal where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, foreign travel advisories, X markers barred, exclusion from government-funded single-sex facilities nationwide, documented transgender immigration-custody abuse, and conversion-therapy-style federal prison policy. A visitor's home passport still faces consular adjudication; state protections don't reach federal buildings, custody, or entry. For travelling families, under-18 care is paused at two hospital systems under federal funding pressure.

entry_documents.exposure: 24 Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal where documents/records show discrepancy or 'reasonable doubt' on applicant's sex, with possible referral to a fraud-based lifetime ineligibility finding; X markers no longer issued; trans travellers report passports blocked/confiscated; eight-plus foreign governments issued travel advisories and detentions over visa issues are documented.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waiver options; existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; the policy is under active national litigation and several related orders are enjoined; visitors present home-country passports rather than applying for local recognition.
entry_documents.interaction: Consular adjudication abroad and federal entry screening occur before any state-level tolerance is reached; a document mismatch can also trigger secondary screening, device checks and outing at security, and could colour later state encounters such as hotel check-in or police ID checks.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented immigration-custody abuse of transgender men: forced-labour programmes with guards saying 'I'll treat you like a man', beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. From 2026 the federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for transgender inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal, substitute psychiatric drugs); transgender prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: This state has no facility or sex-definition law, so the documented bathroom-trespass arrest model does not operate locally; state prisoners retain a court-enforced right to hormone therapy (2011 appellate ruling, 2012 cert denial); federal custody policies are challenged in court.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor's state-level arrest can migrate into federal custody or immigration detention, where the hostile federal policies apply regardless of the state's own posture; document discrepancy at entry is the pathway most likely to trigger detention at all.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The 20 January 2025 executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity nationwide, covering federal buildings inside this state; nationally 22-plus units have facility bans, six extend to private settings, and four make use a criminal offence in some circumstances (one documented arrest, 19 March 2025, held 24 hours in a men's ward).
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state has no law barring facility use consistent with gender identity, no law defining sex to exclude transgender people, and no drag ban; a 2019 executive order bars discrimination in state employment, contracting and state services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Within the same city a visitor may be welcome in a state building and excluded from the federal building next door; the equality map warns other state laws or policies defining sex may affect access beyond mapped bans.

care_services.exposure: Two major hospital systems paused gender-affirming pharmacologic care for under-18s on 13 January 2026 after the federal health department threatened to deny public insurance payments; proposed federal rules would bar public insurance reimbursement for trans under-18s; national LGBTQ youth crisis services were shut down in July 2025.
care_services.protection: The state bars no gender-affirming care, has no youth-care ban (governor vetoed one in December 2023 and a sports bill in April 2024), the state lawyer joined a multistate challenge to the federal declaration, and private and public insurance may not exclude transgender-specific care; prison hormone therapy is protected.
care_services.interaction: Federal funding pressure overrides state policy at hospitals receiving federal funds, so a state-level protection does not deliver care to a visiting minor; whether the January 2026 pause still applies is not sourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal framing treats trans advocacy as security threat-adjacent: a December 2025 reward memorandum lists 'radical gender ideology' among extreme viewpoints, a May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names groups 'radically pro-transgender', an executive order calls youth care 'mutilation' and directs law-enforcement investigation of schools; 66% nationally support sex-at-birth document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward is expressly not conditioned on gender ideology and the strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target those who merely disagree; the state's governor publicly pledged to veto any bill making the state less inclusive, and an independent July 2026 assessment places it in the low-risk group.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing elevates the ambient hostility a visibly trans visitor meets even in this state, and can colour how quickly officers escalate a document discrepancy into an investigation.

minors_guardians.exposure: Executive order directs law enforcement to criminally prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; youth-care pause at two state hospital systems under federal funding pressure; proposed federal insurance bar for trans under-18s; 27 units ban youth care and many bar trans students from facilities, though not this state.
minors_guardians.protection: This state bans neither youth care nor drag, the governor vetoed the care ban, the state joined the challenge, marriage and parenting rules are inclusive, and birth certificates offer gender-neutral parent options.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor may need care that state hospitals have paused federally, and the child's documents can trigger the same entry scrutiny as an adult's; no minor-specific entry protocol is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide gender-identity discrimination ban and gender identity is not a protected class in the state hate-crime statute (sexual orientation is); prosecutors have sometimes used perceived sexual orientation as the route to charge gender-identity-motivated crimes, without documented case counts. Local coverage is patchwork: 21% of the population in ten full-ordinance cities, 12% partial.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Sexual-orientation discrimination has been banned statewide since 1982; a national hate-crime statute covers gender identity and national employment discrimination law covers it; a city police department stopped listing victim gender in 2023; advocacy infrastructure and a 2017 poll showing 73% support for a gender-identity nondiscrimination law indicate social acceptance.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Outside ordinance cities a visitor's practical recourse for service refusal or harassment narrows to federal channels, which are politically contested; absence of documented attacks is a partly silent record rather than proof of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Litigation is unresolved: passport suit, executive-order challenges and proposed health rules all pending, so exposure varies by travel date; state equality-map profile is current only to 29 May 2025; no statewide gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage; the low-risk grouping's methodology is unpublished.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several federal orders, a legal-aid organisation maintains a running passport-rules FAQ, the state AG litigates against the federal care rule, and the July 2026 assessment places the state among units 'largely refrained from targeting transgender adults'.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Which rules are operative depends on forum: entry and federal-building questions resolve under contested federal policy, while state fora have been reliable, producing uneven outcomes across a single trip.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars and removes transgender visitors routinely with no remedy. This jurisdiction's entry regime (discrepancy-based refusal, possible lifetime fraud bar, foreign advisories) is comparably exclusionary and worse in tail severity, but is contested in court and waivers exist; crucially, daily life in this state has no register, reporting duty or monitoring regime, so the whole-jurisdiction universal exposure of 0.35-A is absent.

Kestrel Isles offers extended secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow, rarely successful appeals — a close match to this dossier's entry axis, which adds a possible lifetime ineligibility finding. This jurisdiction scores below 0.55-B because it layers federal facility exclusion, documented immigration-custody abuse and official threat-framing on top of that screening; state tolerance softens but does not cancel those federal exposures.

Meridia trains border officers, recognises diverse markers, and detentions end in release with counsel and compensation. That is materially above this dossier: here markers are restricted, refusal is instructed on sex-doubt grounds, multiple governments issued advisories, and custody carries documented abuse. The state's low-risk profile narrows the gap but cannot lift the combined regime into the 0.75 band.

Drellia's mandatory registration and nightly hotel transmission create continuous discovery exposure with slow, secretive remedies. This jurisdiction lacks that universal daily registration machinery, which argues above 0.45; but Drellia lacks documented custodial abuse and nationwide facility exclusion, which the federal layer here supplies, keeping the two close.

parsed.synthesis: The state is genuinely non-targeting: no facility or sex-definition law, vetoed care and sports bans, a 2019 inclusive executive order, 1982 sexual-orientation protections, protected prison hormone therapy, marriage recognition, tolerant polling, and a July 2026 low-risk grouping — but no statewide gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage, so local remedies are patchwork. The federal layer governs the journey's hard points: visa adjudication instructed to refuse on sex doubt with a possible lifetime fraud bar, foreign travel advisories, exclusion from government-funded single-sex facilities, documented transgender immigration-custody abuse, conversion-therapy-style federal prison policy, and under-18 care paused by funding threats. Litigation is pending but does not protect a traveller on a given date. Severity is bounded — no criminalisation of identity here, functioning courts that have won injunctions — so this sits mid-scale: elevated by universal federal exposures, lifted by an unusually protective state.
